The Barr body is the transcriptionally inactive, highly condensed X chromosome that appears as a dense, darkly staining mass in the nucleus of female mammalian cells. This condensed, transcription‑silent state is the hallmark of **heterochromatin** (specifically, facultative heterochromatin, because an otherwise active chromosome is silenced in certain cells).
